questions.question: A metal spoon, a wooden table, and a plastic cup are left in a classroom overnight. What can we say about their temperatures in the morning?
options: The metal spoon will be much colder than the wooden table.
All three objects will have reached the same temperature as the room.
The plastic cup will be warmer than the metal spoon.
The wooden table will have stayed at its original temperature.

questions.question: What happens to the particles inside a metal bar when it is heated?
options: They stop moving entirely and lock into position.
They start to slide past each other and flow.
They vibrate more quickly about their fixed positions.
They turn into gas particles and escape immediately.

questions.question: When a liquid is heated, what happens to the spacing between its particles?
options: The particles get closer together.
The separation of the particles increases.
The particles stay exactly the same distance apart.
The particles disappear, leaving empty spaces.

questions.question: Why does the liquid level in a thermometer rise when it is placed in hot water?
options: The heating causes the liquid to expand.
The liquid gets heavier and pushes upwards.
The liquid contracts and takes up less space.
The glass tube shrinks and squeezes the liquid up.

questions.question: How does the movement of particles in a cup of hot tea at 80°C compare to a cup of warm tea at 40°C?
options: The particles in the 80°C tea are moving faster on average.
The particles in the 80°C tea are moving slower on average.
The particles in both cups are moving at exactly the same speed.
The particles in the 80°C tea have stopped moving.

questions.question: A mug of boiling water at 95°C and a mug of warm water at 40°C are placed in a room at 20°C. Which mug will cool down fastest at the very beginning?
options: The 40°C mug, because it is closer to room temperature.
Both mugs will cool down at the exact same rate.
The 95°C mug, because the temperature difference between it and the air is greater.
Neither mug will cool down because the room is too warm.

questions.question: Two different materials of the same mass are heated with the same energy. One heats up very quickly, while the other heats up very slowly. What does this demonstrate?
options: All materials require the same amount of energy to change temperature.
It is easier to increase the temperature of some materials than others.
The material that heated up slowly is a better thermal conductor.
The material that heated up quickly must have a higher mass.

questions.question: Why do different substances have different thermal properties, such as needing different amounts of heating to raise their temperature?
options: Some substances do not contain any particles at all.
The mass of particles and the attractive forces between them vary in different substances.
All substances have identical particles, but some are packed tighter.
Particles in some substances never move when heated.

questions.question: If Substance A has a higher specific heat capacity than Substance B, what is true about 1 kg of each substance at 50°C?
options: Substance A has more energy in its thermal store than Substance B.
Substance B has more energy in its thermal store than Substance A.
Both substances contain the same amount of energy because their masses are equal.
Neither substance contains any energy because they are at the same temperature.

questions.question: In which states of matter do the particles move in random directions?
options: Gases only.
Liquids and gases only.
Solids, liquids, and gases.
Solids and liquids only.

questions.question: You have two identical iron blocks, Block X and Block Y. Block X is at 80°C and Block Y is at 30°C. Which block has more energy in its thermal store?
options: Block Y, because cooler objects store more energy.
Block X, because for identical objects, the one at a higher temperature has more energy.
They both have the same energy because they are identical blocks.
Neither block has any energy because they are solid.

questions.question: A small cup of water at 60°C and a large bucket of water at 60°C are compared. Which contains more energy in its thermal store?
options: The small cup, because the heat is more concentrated.
They contain the same energy because they are at the same temperature.
The large bucket, because it has more particles and therefore more energy.
The large bucket, because water in a bucket is always hotter than in a cup.

questions.question: How should you position your eyes to take an accurate reading from a glass thermometer?
options: Look down at the thermometer from directly above.
Position your eye so it is level with the top of the coloured liquid.
Tilt the thermometer towards you and read it from a 45-degree angle.
Look up at the thermometer from below the liquid line.

questions.question: What are the melting and boiling points of pure water under normal conditions?
options: Melts at 0ºC, boils at 100ºC.
Melts at 10ºC, boils at 100ºC.
Melts at 0ºC, boils at 50ºC.
Melts at -10ºC, boils at 110ºC.

questions.question: If you mix a cup of hot water at 80°C with a cup of cold water at 10°C, what will the final temperature of the mixture be?
options: It will stay exactly at 80°C.
It will drop to below 10°C.
It will be cooler than 80°C but warmer than 10°C.
It will rise above 80°C because of the mixing energy.

questions.question: If you mix 1 litre of cold water at 10°C with a tiny splash (10 ml) of boiling water at 100°C, what will the final temperature be closest to?
options: It will be very close to 10°C, because there was much more cold water.
It will be exactly 55°C, the halfway point.
It will be very close to 100°C, because boiling water is stronger.
It will be 0°C, because mixing always drops the temperature.

questions.question: What happens to the movement of particles when a cold metal spoon is placed into a hot bowl of soup?
options: The soup particles move more quickly and the spoon particles move more slowly.
The soup particles move more slowly and the spoon particles move more quickly.
The particles in both the spoon and the soup stop moving.
There is no change in the movement of particles in either substance.

questions.question: What happens to the temperature along a thermal conductor, like a copper rod, when one end is heated?
options: The temperature along the conductor increases very slowly.
The temperature along the conductor increases quickly.
Only the heated end changes temperature; the rest remains freezing cold.
The temperature drops instantly along the entire rod.

questions.question: Why is heat transferred very slowly through thermal insulators?
options: Thermal insulators do not contain any particles that can vibrate.
The particles in thermal insulators are too large to move at all.
It is hard for vibrating particles in insulators to cause nearby particles to vibrate as well.
Insulators only allow particles to move in one straight direction.

questions.question: Why does a woollen jumper keep you warm on a cold day?
options: Wool produces its own heat energy through a chemical reaction.
It traps air, and gases are very poor thermal conductors, which provides good insulation.
The jumper allows cold air to pass through quickly to cool your skin.
Wool has zero particles, so heat cannot move through it.
